clue.text: Little lad, one flogging camera?

parts.note: someone who flogs or lashes is a whipper
snapper is informal for a camera, the thing that snaps pictures

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a small boy who whips and also wields a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that SNAPPER for camera is a loose, playful equation.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an impudent young person, a cheeky small boy.

clue.text: County choristers were discordant

indicators.note: singers who are discordant are out of tune with one another, so the letters of the words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A county's choir sang out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discordant' is the anagram signal; the letters of 'choristers were' are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcestershire is a county in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: Patients or prisoners at home with friends

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
mates are friends

explanation.surface: Hospital patients or jail prisoners spending time at home with their friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates are people confined in an institution, whether hospital, asylum or prison.

clue.text: Mobile phone and chemical company once — one in Dido's homeland

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters of the next word are moved around

parts.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a British chemical company, broken up in 2008
a means one

explanation.surface: A list of a mobile phone, an old chemical firm and a classical queen's home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' reads as a single gadget, but 'Mobile' is the anagram signal on PHONE, giving PHOEN.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Dido, founder of Carthage, came from Tyre in Phoenicia on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: He's kept busy stocktaking

parts.note: stocktaking reads as counting a shop's inventory, but here it means taking (stealing) livestock

explanation.surface: A busy man tallying a shop's goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here is cattle and taking is stealing, so the busy man is a thief of farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is a thief who steals cattle, horses or sheep.

clue.text: Unavoidable fate of Tyneside canteen, I gathered

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: the canteen has gathered up the I, holding it within

parts.note: a mess is a canteen, as in a military dining hall

explanation.surface: A doomed Tyneside canteen, so the speaker understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' poses as 'I understood'; in fact the mess gathers I inside it, making MESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis, named after the Greek goddess of retribution, is a downfall that cannot be escaped.

clue.text: These shallow waters upset sailing boat

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sloop is a single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Shallow water capsizing a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: Pools are small, still, shallow bodies of water, such as those left by the tide.

clue.text: Studio location of horror film with final bits cut

indicators.note: the final letters of each word of the title are cut off

parts.note: A Nightmare on Elm Street is a famous horror film, shortened here to Elm Street

explanation.surface: Where a horror film was shot, released with its ending trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with final bits cut' drops the last letter of each word, M from ELM and T from STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree in Hertfordshire is home to well-known film and television studios near London.

clue.text: Book a week in it, local resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday week at a nearby seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination but is read as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Town Like Alice is a 1950 novel by Nevil Shute, set partly in Malaya and Australia.

clue.text: Wild garlic from butts above square

parts.note: to butt is to ram with the head, so butts means rams
on means upon or above

explanation.surface: Wild garlic that is gathered from the cask ends set over a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsons is a woodland plant, Allium ursinum, also called bear's garlic.

clue.text: Second attack when night becomes even darker?

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
an onset is an attack or assault

explanation.surface: A second assault launched under cover of a deepening night.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonset is the time the moon goes below the horizon, removing its light from the night sky.

clue.text: Chairs lacking covers, so get a takeaway

indicators.note: the covers are the outer letters, which are removed

parts.note: chairs collectively are seating

explanation.surface: A restaurant with no free tables, so order food to go instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Covers in a restaurant are diners' places, but here they are the word's outer letters. To eat in also means to dine at home, as you do with a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal at home rather than going out, typically with a takeaway.

clue.text: Endures temperature — bitterly cold — at breaking point

parts.note: lasts means endures
raw weather is bitterly cold

explanation.surface: Someone putting up with freezing weather until they can take no more.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the final burden that makes something unbearable, the point where patience gives way.

clue.text: Seen on TV, they provide details of Ashes scores

definitions.meaning: ... were images broadcast on TV when no programme was showing

definitions.text: they provide details of Ashes scores
definitions.meaning: the Ashes is the England v Australia cricket Test series, and a Test match's scorecards are its cards

explanation.surface: Things shown on television that report scores from the Ashes cricket series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia, so scorecards from it are Test cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A test card is a still pattern broadcast for tuning sets; a cricket scorecard is a card for a Test match.

clue.text: Dandy that's experienced at sea

definitions.meaning: the long rolling movement of the sea felt aboard ship

explanation.surface: A fashionable man who is a seasoned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell names both a stylish gentleman and the heaving of ocean waves.

clue.text: Repository for wrecked car (rear end missing), perhaps

indicators.note: a wrecked car is smashed up, so these letters are broken and rearranged
the last letter of car is missing

explanation.surface: Where a smashed car with its back end gone might end up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear end missing' trims car to CA; CA plus PERHAPS is then rearranged by 'wrecked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a dump where discarded things, such as wrecked cars, are stored.

clue.text: Sources of Riesling in Oppenheim — just any wine?

indicators.note: the sources of words are their opening letters, taken from each word in turn

explanation.surface: Asking whether Riesling from the German wine town of Oppenheim is just any old wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: East German's wealthy bird

parts.note: the German word for east is Ost
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A rich East German's bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person from the old GDR, but it means the word for east in German.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird.

clue.text: Wind power in green area creating red tape

indicators.note: the twisted letters go inside the green area

parts.note: a park is a green area

indicators.note: wind as a verb means twist, so the letters of power are twisted around

explanation.surface: Wind energy turbines in a park generating bureaucracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind power' reads as renewable energy; 'Wind' is a verb that twists POWER into PERWO.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive official forms and paperwork, the routine documents of bureaucracy.

clue.text: Publicity broadcast that is plain

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
to air is to broadcast
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Publicity that is broadcast is plain speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open grassland, a plain, especially in North America.

clue.text: Marked on the map, as the conspirator did

definitions.meaning: to plot is to mark a position on a map or chart

explanation.surface: A route marked on a map by a scheming plotter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotted means both charted on paper and secretly schemed.

clue.text: Outdoor work — drop of early rain affected

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: a drop of a word is a small part of it, its first letter
affected means altered, so the letters of rain are changed in order

explanation.surface: Outdoor work spoiled by an early spot of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something taking place outside rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Awkward matter with sexy Charlotte?

parts.note: hot means sexy
Charlotte is a popular variety of potato

explanation.surface: An embarrassing situation involving an attractive woman named Charlotte.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte looks like a woman's name; it is a salad potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is a controversial issue that is hard to handle.

clue.text: Dominant leg-spinner

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A commanding leg-spin bowler in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg-spinner is a type of cricket bowler; split, 'leg' is ON, the leg side of the field, and 'spinner' is a top.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on top is to be winning or in control.

clue.text: Mondrian and a painting of the BVM

parts.note: the Dutch abstract painter Mondrian's first name supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A Mondrian canvas of the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is an image of the Blessed Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: Go wild — aggro is terrifying inside

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words aggro is terrifying

explanation.surface: Run riot, as the aggressive mood within is frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily and boisterously.

clue.text: Those bearing gifts to mother — encircled by pieces of eight

indicators.note: mother is encircled, wrapped round, by the jumbled letters
the word eight is broken into pieces and reassembled

parts.note: ma is mother

explanation.surface: Gift-bearers bringing pirate coins to their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of eight' reads as old Spanish coins, but 'pieces of' breaks EIGHT into THEGI, which encircles MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi are the wise men who brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Pastor encourages English weed

parts.note: a pastor is a shepherd of his flock
spurs means encourages

explanation.surface: A minister urges on a feeble English person.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's purse is a common small white-flowered plant regarded as a garden weed.
